claim: Greedy compression-guided search finds the answer almost always on the first pass: 54 of 69 MADIL solutions come from the first greedy rollout and 80% appear within 20 s of a 180 s budget; best model has mean rank 1.3.
agent_test: Give the agent a fixed coding scheme; compare first-greedy-pick accuracy to best-of-N at equal tokens.

claim: A short description is a strong selector among fitting candidates: MADIL generalisation among train-fitting models is 82% (57/69), BARC-style programs have about 9% fit-but-wrong, CompressARC beats a same-data U-Net 20% vs 0.75%. Caveat (gap search): no study compares length-based with accuracy-based or vote selection among fitting LLM programs, so the 'short beats random' part rests on MADIL and BARC.
agent_test: Among candidates that pass all examples, pick the shortest under a stated coding scheme versus random pick; same tokens.

claim: Fitting all training pairs is not enough: spurious expressions that patch a wrong decomposition cause fit-but-wrong, worse with fewer examples and larger expression budgets (21 training tasks in MADIL; 7 to 12 tasks gap in 2021 versions; 9% in BARC).
agent_test: Count fit-but-wrong rate with and without a cap on rule size; require hold-out check on one example.

claim: Rehearsal weighting is needed: data term multiplied by 10 (2021) then 100 (2025) because ~3.3 pairs stand for many; too low stops search early, too high overfits. Removing it loses 6 of 71 tasks.
agent_test: Vary weight of fit versus rule size in the agent's scoring prompt; measure accuracy.

claim: Sampling several candidate descriptions of each input matters most in MADIL: Np=1 loses 19 of 71 tasks, Se=1 loses 27; Np=10 vs 100 loses 1.
agent_test: Generate 1 vs several parses of the task before choosing; equal tokens.

claim: MDL search and brute-force DSL search solve different tasks: on eval, MADIL 59, Icecuber 117, overlap 43, MADIL-only 16.
agent_test: Run two selectors and union; check complementarity.

claim: Pure MDL/DSL systems stay well below fine-tuned LLM ensembles: MADIL 7% private, CompressARC 20% public eval, Icecuber 17-20%, BARC+TTT ensembles 56.75-61.9%, PoE 71.6% (public eval).
agent_test: Baseline context only; compare at equal tokens.

claim: Induction (program) and transduction (direct output) solve different tasks, stable across seeds; ensembling beats either: BARC 56.75% ensemble vs 43.25% best single on ARC-Heavy.
agent_test: Run both modes on same tasks and fall back from program to direct answer when no program fits.

claim: Test-time training lifts neural ARC solvers sharply: 18.3% to 47.1% (8B fine-tuned), 53.0% on BARC base, 61.9% ensembled; PoE selection and augmented views push to 71.6%. Semi-private score was lower (47.5%).
agent_test: Not testable without training; use augmented re-presentation of the task as a prompt-only analog.

claim: Scoring candidates by total log-probability across augmented views (product of experts) is a code-length-like selector and adds about 5 points over sampling-probability top-2 (62.5 to 67.6% on 8B).
agent_test: Rank candidates by summed likelihood across rephrased/transformed task views.

claim: LLM hypothesis-then-program works better than direct programs, but selection of the right hypothesis is the bottleneck: GPT-4 direct 17%, program 23%, summarised hypotheses 30%, human-picked 33%, only 49 tasks had a correct hypothesis.
agent_test: Generate natural-language hypotheses first, execute each as code on examples, then select.

claim: Test-time compression without pretraining works partly: CompressARC 76K parameters, 2000 steps, 20 min, 20% eval and 34.75% train (pass@2); accuracy rises with steps but eval pass@2 peaks at 1500 steps (21.5%) then dips.
agent_test: Not an LLM test; treat as ceiling for pure MDL.

claim: MDL systems have stated structural blind spots: no conditionals or recursion (MADIL), cannot count, repeat serially, rotate or extend long-range patterns (CompressARC); 21 of 62 MADIL search failures need non-compressive intermediate steps.
agent_test: Allow a non-shortest step in search; test on tasks needing detours.

claim: Search-over-DSL approaches collapse on ARC-AGI-2: Icecuber 17.0% to 1.6%, o3 medium 53.0% to 3.0%, ARChitects 56.0% to 2.5%; benchmark designed against brute force; pooled 2020 entries solved 49% of private ARC-AGI-1.
agent_test: Boundary condition: report both ARC-AGI-1 and 2.

claim: Humans: ARC-AGI-1 task accuracy after 3 attempts 76.2% train, 64.2% eval (H-ARC, 784/948 participants); the earlier 83.8% came from a 40-task sample. Longer rule descriptions predicted lower solve rate.
agent_test: Human baseline for calibrating agent scores.

claim: Learned program priors compete with MDL priors: GridCoder (learned probability model, enumerate in probability order) 5.75% eval at 15 min, 79.3% of DSL-solvable tasks; CodeIt 15% eval with hindsight relabelling and shorter programs found for 53% of solved tasks.
agent_test: Compare learned likelihood to length as a selector.

claim: No independent replication of MADIL exists in opened sources; all MADIL figures are one author's. Table 6 eval figure (15.1%) is reconstructed from a garbled table; 57 to 59 of 400 (14.25-14.75%) is consistent. Gap search 2026-10: a survey of 82 approaches and the CompressARC citer list show no independent re-run; the MADIL citer list could not be retrieved (API limits).
agent_test: Treat MADIL numbers as provisional.

claim: Among LLM programs that already fit all training pairs, picking the right one is a smaller bottleneck than generating a right one: selection by training accuracy recovers about 95% of the 5-candidate ceiling (ARC-AGI-1, DeepSeek V3.2); on ARC-AGI-2 with 8-29 candidates, 22 of 167 instances had no correct candidate and 17 had one that was not picked.
agent_test: Measure the oracle gap (any candidate right vs chosen candidate right) before adding a length selector; add one only if the gap is large.

claim: Consensus is a poor selector on hard ARC tasks: a trace-reading judge beat majority vote by 7 solved instances, all minority recoveries (ARC-AGI-2 public, GPT-5.2); a lone correct program against 12 and 8 agreeing wrong ones; dedup of convergent outputs is used to protect dissenters. Majority voting also sits 9.5 points below the oracle in SOAR.
agent_test: Compare majority vote, dedup-by-output, and shortest-rule pick on tasks where the modal answer is wrong.

claim: No ARC Prize 2025 Kaggle winner is described as using MDL or code length for selection; the one MDL system (CompressARC) won a paper award, with 20% ARC-AGI-1 and 4% ARC-AGI-2. Winners used test-time training, synthetic data and likelihood scoring over augmented views.
agent_test: Context only; the technical report is a summary and team write-ups were not opened.

claim: A prompt-only analogue of compression helps frozen LLMs on ARC-AGI-2: induce a short schema and rule, then pass only that to later stages in fresh contexts. Gains over self-refine: +8.7/+14.0 (GPT-5.5) and +8.0/+9.8 (Gemini 3.1 Pro) at pass@1/pass@5. The same structured output inside one context is worse than the baseline.
agent_test: Rule-first with context reset versus rule-first in one context; equal tokens.

claim: Length-weighted ranking of LLM hypotheses has only an anecdote-scale test: 3 Mini-ARC tasks, Solomonoff-style score vs accuracy-only BMA gave 64 vs 48, 100 vs 100, 60 vs 64 percent. No result either way.
agent_test: A proper test needs hundreds of tasks and a program-length (not text-length) measure.

claim: Open: no measured test of MDL or code-length selection for LLM-written ARC programs at matched sampling cost (gap 1), no flat-prior ablation of MADIL (gap 4), no length-vs-correctness study of reasoning traces (gap 7), no description-length analysis on H-ARC (gap 8). Searches this session found none.
agent_test: These are experiments we would have to run ourselves.

claim: Guards against fit-but-wrong in LLM programs that are in use (the existence of the guards is established; their effect is not): reject programs that contain training outputs as literals (SOAR); forbid colour-keyed if-else patches in repair prompts (Hourglass); require all training pairs exact and dedup by test output (Moghe and Chin). None is ablated alone, so effect sizes are unknown.
agent_test: Ablate each guard separately on a 100-task sample.
